- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 2–3% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven support.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 7 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.0–0.2 values (e.g., 3+ consecutive), model tends to drift downward; apply upward correction of 1–3% to counteract mean reversion bias.  
- If forecast and true outcome diverge >10% in first 3 days, adjust horizon-specific weights: reduce weight on early days (1–3) if sentiment is negative, increase if positive.
